fixes.instruction: Publish an SPF record for this domain that lists every service that sends its mail.
Rotate the DKIM key to 2,048 bits: a key under 1,024 bits is rejected by receivers.

note: Open: the bands call `dmarc_policy_none` acceptable, as they do whenever an SPF or DKIM fix is open. The call is that it is wrong here: there is no SPF record and the only DKIM key is too short for receivers to accept, so no message can pass DMARC at all, and the bounces at 4.1% and the grade falling to low show receivers already refusing some of this mail. A client who acts on a warning about p=none would have all of its own mail quarantined or rejected. With one of the two working the bands' answer would stand; with neither, staying at p=none is the correct state until both fixes are done. The other types follow the bands. It rests on the DMARC RFC, under which a message passes only when SPF or DKIM passes in alignment.
